title: Page 100 — four arrangements
question: Page 100 is pinned. These are four arrangements of its teletext grammar for your 85-inch 4K: no HOME banner, no inputs on this screen (they live on their own page, P110), no status clutter, and a denser, smaller scale. Pick the arrangement — or steer.

options.label: P100 · Index grid
options.lineage: teletext index page (the P100 front page itself)
options.thesis: Six numbered blocks, nothing else: the front page exactly as teletext indexes a service.
options.viewport: Clock double-height top-left as the headline; six flat numbered blocks filling the page; colour-key command line at the foot; P110 INPUTS as a tiny page number bottom-right.
options.risk: Six blocks alone can feel bare at 85-inch scale if the rhythm wobbles.

options.label: P100 · Rows
options.lineage: teletext A-Z service menus (numbered rows, inverted selection)
options.thesis: Favorites as a numbered list — the teletext menu page: scan the column, land on a number.
options.viewport: Six rows, each: yellow block number, white one-word name, thin rule; the selected row renders as an inverted blue block across the column; clock inline at top-right; P110 cue in the footer.
options.risk: Lists read slower than blocks; the number becomes decoration if the names dominate.

options.label: P100 · Mosaic
options.lineage: teletext feature pages (asymmetric colour panels, sport-page layout)
options.thesis: A colour-field mosaic where block size says priority — the two you watch most take double panels.
materials: white block type on saturated panels
options.viewport: Two double-width panels (YouTube, Netflix) over four singles; page numbers burned into each panel corner; clock as a narrow headline strip across the top; footer carries only colour keys and P110.
options.risk: Colour fields at 85 inches are loud; wrong panel size and priority becomes noise.

options.label: P100 · Clock page
options.lineage: teletext clock/newsflash pages (giant four-character time as the page's headline)
options.thesis: The time is the page's headline — glance mode: what's the time, what's pinned, done.
options.viewport: 21:47 rendered as enormous double-height yellow block numerals across the upper half; one compact row of six small numbered blocks beneath; date and LIVE status as a single micro line; P110 cue in the footer.
options.risk: Clock-first makes favorites secondary furniture — wrong bet if you launch more than you glance.
